summary: Harry Falk specializes in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He held posts at the University of Freiburg (~1979–1993), Humboldt University of Berlin, and served as professor at the Free University of Berlin (2005–2010).

Hartmut Buescher works in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Copenhagen (~1998–2003) under Chandrabhal Tripathi, Claus Oetke, Tom J. F. Tillemans, and Eli Franco, and held posts at Copenhagen and the Royal Danish Library.
Hartmut Scharfe was an Indologist and linguist who earned his doctorate under Paul Thieme (~1953–1956). He held a post at the University of California, Los Angeles, until 1961.

Hartmut-Ortwin Feistel is an Indologist. He served in the Oriental Department of the Berlin State Library (~1979–2006) and held a project leadership and editorial post at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities.
Haruhiko Masaki is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He completed his master's coursework at the University of Tokyo by ~1968 and served as a professor at Nagasaki University.
Haruka Yanagisawa was an Indologist and historian. He held academic posts at Chiba University (~1978–1990) and the University of Tokyo (~1990–2007).

Harumi Hirano Ziegler specializes in Buddhist studies. She completed an MA at the University of California, Los Angeles (~1994–2001), studying under Robert E. Buswell Jr., William M. Bodiford, and Richard von Glahn.

Harunaga Isaacson works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied at Groningen and Leiden, held posts at Groningen, Oxford, and Pennsylvania (2002–2006), and became professor at the University of Hamburg (2000–2016).
Harushige Kōzu was a linguist who studied at the University of Oxford (~1937–1939). He subsequently held posts at the University of Tokyo (~1947–1969) and Musashi University (~1969–1973).

Harvey B. Aronson specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Richard Hugh Robinson among others, served as professor at the University of Virginia (~1978–1984), and became co-director of Dawn Mountain Center for Tibetan Buddhism (~1996).
Haya Akegarasu was a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies. He studied at Otani University from 1896 to 1900 and at the Tokyo School of Foreign Languages in 1900.
Heather Stoddard specializes in Tibetology and history and archaeology. She studied at SOAS University of London (~1966–1970) and under D. C. Lau, Samten Gyaltsen Karmay, and Nicole Vandier-Nicolas.
Hegoda Khemananda was a scholar of Buddhist studies. He served as Vice Principal at Vidyodaya Pirivena and as Director at Dharma Paryeshanalaya.

Heidi Fjeld is a Tibetologist who studied at Oxford (2002) and completed her doctorate under Signe Howell at the University of Oslo (~2001–2006), where she also held a postdoctoral fellowship (~2007–2010).

Heidi I. Koppl specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She completed an MA at the University of Copenhagen under Christian K. Wedemeyer and studied under traditional teacher Khenpo Sherab Zangpo.
Heidi Pauwels is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. She studied at KU Leuven (1983) and earned her PhD at the University of Washington (1994), where she joined the faculty (~1996).
Heinrich Blochmann worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Indology, and history. He studied at Leipzig University (~1855–1857) and the University of Calcutta (~1860–1862).

Heinrich Ewald was a scholar of linguistics, religious studies, and Indology. He studied at the University of Göttingen under Johann Gottfried Eichhorn and held professorships at the University of Tübingen (1838–1848) and Göttingen (1848–1867).

Heinrich Hettrich was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Saarland University (~1969–1974) and the University of Giessen (~1974–1976). He held posts at Munich (~1978–1982), Saarland (~1982–1988), and Würzburg (~1988–2012).

Heinrich Hübschmann was a linguist, Indologist, and Iranian specialist. He studied at the University of Jena (~1868–1872) and under Martin Haug (~1871–1872), later holding a post at Leipzig University (~1876–1877).
